status_policy: a candidate is never promoted to a frozen parameter; UNKNOWN carries the concrete missing measurement

frames.cad: CAD model frame, millimetres, as recorded by the STEP/USD measurement tools
frames.chassis: chassis body frame = R_x(90 deg) . (0.001 * CAD mm); origin = CAD global origin, which is NOT a calibrated chassis datum
frames.up_axis_note: the mapping sends the geometric vertical (CAD y) to chassis z, which agrees with the USD stage upAxis = Z; this RESOLVES the PR #25 up-axis conflict as a candidate, and still is not a vendor statement

axle_line_cad.line_form: point + t * direction, t in millimetres, unrestricted
axle_line_cad.why: direction is measured three independent ways; the point is a measured wheel centre, but the CAD global origin is not a chassis datum
axle_line_cad.frame: CAD model frame (global origin, +x = spin axis family)
axle_line_cad.sign_note: the stored CIRCLE placement axis is (+1,0,0) on the +x wheels and (-1,0,0) on the -x wheels: an axle line is unsigned, and the flip is itself mirror evidence, never a spin direction

axle_line_chassis.why: the CAD->USD mapping (0.001 scale + 90 deg about x) is documented and applied, but the chassis frame origin/up axis are not vendor-authorized, so chassis-frame values stay candidates
axle_line_chassis.frame: chassis body frame = R_x(90 deg) . (0.001 * CAD mm), Z-up

residual.note: the mapping is a similarity (orthogonal + uniform 0.001), so it cannot change the path residual: the two paths differ by the CAD-frame 0.002 mm centre offset, which is 2e-06 m after the transform

outward_axle_direction.spin_convention: omega_vector = spin_sign * (v_roll / r) * x_hat gives a wheel rolling with +v_roll along chassis -y; the forward direction itself is UNKNOWN

residual.note: all four solids are parallel to chassis x to 0.0043 deg (PCA) / 0.165 deg (min-span scan); the outward sign is assigned exactly by the sign of the measured chassis x of the centre
the surface type is analytic, so there is no tessellation residual; the only residual is between the torus equator and the independently measured circle

classification.value: TOROIDAL_SURFACE crowned tread band (two torus faces per axial half, 180 deg major each)
classification.why: every face bounding the 103 mm edge circle is an analytic TOROIDAL_SURFACE with major radius 77.738 mm and minor radius 25.262 mm; no cylindrical face of that radius exists in the solid
classification.frame: CAD BREP (analytic surface entities, no tessellation involved)

tread_geometry.frame: CAD model frame, axial band along the wheel spin axis through the wheel centre

residual.area_method: torus integral r*[R*dtheta_minor + r*sin] * dtheta_major, dtheta from the face's own circular edges
residual.area_method_limit: the major-angle coverage comes from circle-arc sums; a face trimmed by a spline rather than circles would be under-counted

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: the rolling surface is the 103 mm edge's adjacent cylinder
rejected_hypotheses.evidence: the largest cylindrical face radius in each wheel solid is 68.5 mm; there is no cylinder at 92.5 mm or 103 mm

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: the rolling surface is a 49 mm wide flat cylindrical tread
rejected_hypotheses.evidence: the 103 mm circle is the equator of a torus; the tread band spans a 41.0 mm axial band but the radius drops to 92.5 mm at its edges

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: the wheel is a plain disc with a 206 mm flange
rejected_hypotheses.evidence: radial band 92.5 -> 103.0 mm on a 41 mm wide torus; the flange hypothesis predicted a planar annulus, and the total planar area per wheel is only 1883.2 mm^2

track_width.why: measured relative geometry in the chassis frame; the frame origin and the steering pose remain unauthorised
track_width.frame: chassis body frame, lateral = chassis x (CAD x)

wheelbase.why: same as track_width; note the wheelbase is along chassis y, which is CAD z, not chassis z
wheelbase.frame: chassis body frame, fore-aft = chassis y (CAD z)

wheel_centre_plane_spread.why: all four measured wheel centres share one chassis z plane to the measurement resolution; this is what lets a single lift constant be well defined

unloaded_rolling_height_from_geometry.why: chassis z of the wheel centre plus the 103 mm unloaded equatorial radius; the loaded rolling radius stays UNKNOWN

part_identity.verdict: mirrored pairs (left / right), not four identical parts
part_identity.status: verified at the BREP face-signature level, candidate for the physical part number
part_identity.why: the tread torus is split into two 180 deg faces whose axial bands are [-20.502, -0.002] and [-0.002, 20.498] mm on the +x wheels and sign-flipped on the -x wheels, so the solids are mirror placements, not the same orientation
part_identity.why_not_four_identical: identical parts would show identical axial-band signs in the same CAD frame; they do not

cross_checks.pr25_verdict: within mesh resolution: no real asymmetry provable from the cloud
cross_checks.v2_adds: analytic face-level sign flip, which the cloud could not resolve

may_use_as_TEST_PROXY_parameters.value: (1,0,0) unit, sign per side from outward_axle_direction.spin_sign
may_use_as_TEST_PROXY_parameters.constraint: direction only; use spin_sign, never a hard-coded +/-
relative geometry only; do not treat the origin as a chassis datum
relative geometry only, in the documented chassis mapping
relative geometry only; the wheelbase runs along chassis y
TEST_PROXY only; a loaded rolling radius is UNKNOWN

may_use_as_TEST_PROXY_parameters.value: 0.041 m wide, centred on the wheel plane
may_use_as_TEST_PROXY_parameters.constraint: drives contact-patch width proxies; not a tyre model
sign convention relative to the outward axle; the forward direction remains UNKNOWN

forbidden_as_real_values: wheel_radius as a frozen physical parameter (0.103 m stays a TEST_PROXY)
loaded_rolling_height / any tyre deflection or contact-patch length
lift = 0.334 m (it is 13 mm below the geometric 0.347 m and was never measured)
the 0.090 m proxy collision half-height as a real tread half-width
wheel mass, inertia tensor, friction coefficients, tread compliance
chassis-frame origin as a calibrated datum, or chassis z as an authorised gravity axis
any axle joint axis / motor channel inferred from the axis-cluster recording
steering freedom, steering range or steering-axis position
the toroidal tread as proof of the tyre material or of a real contact model
gates_for_p4: read a field's verdict before using it; UNKNOWN must fail closed
every candidate consumed must be an explicit parameter with a sensitivity sweep
the spin sign must come from outward_axle_direction.spin_sign, not from a constant
no number in this file may be cited as a measured physical wheel property

unknowns.missing_measurement: a loaded contact test (or tyre stiffness + vehicle load) to convert the 103 mm unloaded equator into a rolling radius
the torus only gives the unloaded crown; patch size needs a contact/deflection measurement
a vendor chassis frame declaration or a physical datum calibration (origin + authorised up axis)
which chassis y sign is the front of the vehicle
a joint definition or a measured steering pose sweep
vendor data or a measured part
material specification; the BREP carries no material
